content: That I feed the hungry, that I forgive an insult, that I love my enemy—these are undoubtedly great virtues. But what if I should discover that the least among them all, the poorest of all the beggars, is within me?
author: Carl Jung
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Across his life and work, Carl Jung saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: What defensive wall or grudge are you holding onto that is keeping genuine warmth and intimacy away?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
